item.title: FAA investigates software glitch in some Boeing 737 Max jets
item.description: The FAA is investigating a software glitch in some Boeing 737 Max jets​ that could prompt an automated flight guidance system to disengage during an aborted landing.

item.title: Why Lindsay Clancy's attorney is only now questioning whether she committed killings
item.description: CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down why Lindsay Clancy's attorney might have decided now to question whether she committed the killings of her three children during a hearing on the timing of a potential new trial.

item.title: Winter holiday flight prices reach 10-year high in U.S. as Iran war sends fuel costs soaring
item.description: Winter holiday airfares reached a 10-year high in the U.S. amid Iran war price hikes, a new analysis by Hopper found. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Holiday flight costs hit highest level in a decade
item.description: Flying this holiday season will cost a whole lot more. Kris Van Cleave has details and how to save.

item.title: Video shows students saving their school bus, driver: "Our bus driver just passed out"
item.description: A school bus security camera caught quick-thinking students leaping into action after they noticed the bus driver limp over the steering wheel. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Trump and Rubio question U.K. handling of possible plot against air base
item.description: Rubio claims a possible terror plot against a U.K. air base used by U.S. forces "clearly involved" a foreign actor, but there are few facts to support that.

item.title: Trump and major AI executives sign "morally binding" voluntary controls
item.description: President Trump and the leaders of the country's largest artificial intelligence companies have signed a set of voluntary safety standards, as calls mount for tighter guardrails on powerful AI technology.

item.title: British authorities defend decision to let terror suspects go on bail
item.description: British authorities defended their decision to let a group of young men go free, even as investigators look into a suspected terror plot near an air base there that was used by the U.S. military in its war against Iran. Ramy Inocencio reports from London.

item.title: Trump agrees to let AI leaders police themselves
item.description: President Trump said he sees no need for the government to rein in or slow down artificial intelligence development. After meeting with a group of major tech leaders on Tuesday, he stuck with that position. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's attorney argues for the first time that there's no evidence she killed her kids
item.description: Lindsay Clancy was back in court on Tuesday, her first appearance since a mistrial was declared earlier this month. Clancy's attorney argued for the first time that there is no evidence that Clancy killed her three small children, something he did not dispute in her first trial. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Hegseth to announce a 20% cut to generals and admirals
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is expected to call for a 20% cut in the number of generals and admirals across the U.S. military on Wednesday, a Pentagon official told CBS News.

item.title: Takeaways from Lindsay Clancy court appearance as lawyer questions if Clancy killed her kids
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney cast doubt Tuesday on whether she committed the murders of her three children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has new details.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doel, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Woman in Cornell probe told campus police "I was raped" 3 weeks after alleged incident
item.description: According to a transcript obtained by CBS News New York, the woman identified as Jane Doe said during her interview with Cornell campus police three weeks after the alleged gang rape incident, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." Lilia Luciano reports on more details from the case.

item.title: Iran says it expects response to ceasefire plan already rejected by Trump
item.description: President Trump says U.S. and Iranian negotiators are talking via mediators, but insists he has "offered them NOTHING" to get a peace deal done.

item.title: Trump and tech leaders sign "morally-binding" AI "constitution" in safety push
item.description: President Trump met with key AI leaders at the White House on Tuesday, with the group signing what Mr. Trump called an AI "constitution" aimed at self-policing and safety. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Flash flooding in Southwest, overwhelming New Mexico dam on brink of failing
item.description: Heavy rain drenched portions of the Southwest, putting nearly a third of the country at risk of flash floods in the hours ahead. New Mexico has seen the worst of it so far, where water spilled over a 20-foot dam, prompting emergency crews to urge evacuations. Rob Marciano has more.

item.title: Critics dubbed it California's high-speed rail "anti-transparency bill." A watchdog report reveals why it isn't.
item.description: A watchdog report on wasteful consultant travel became a real-world test of the so-called high-speed rail "anti-transparency" law.

item.title: Attorney says there's "no evidence" Lindsay Clancy admitted killing her kids
item.description: In a surprising turn in Lindsay Clancy's first hearing since her mistrial in early September, her lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued that there was no evidence she killed her kids.

item.title: Princess Diana's brother says Buckingham Palace "has to gaslight" him
item.description: Charles Spencer, the brother of the late Princess Diana, spoke to "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King about writing his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister."

item.title: Taylor Swift to debut "Patient Zero" music video at VMAs. Watch a preview.
item.description: Taylor Swift announced her new single "Patient Zero" earlier this week, saying she has been "impatiently waiting" to announce that it will be out on Friday.

item.title: Charles Spencer on the royal fallout following Princess Diana's death
item.description: In his first interview about his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer talks about his attempt to set down what he calls the definitive story of Princess Diana.

item.title: Porsha Williams reveals health emergency: "It all happened so fast"
item.description: Porsha Williams revealed to "CBS Mornings" co-anchor Gayle King that she had to undergo an emergency partial hysterectomy this year after doctors discovered 21 uterine fibroids

item.title: Oprah reveals new details about live shows coming to Las Vegas Sphere
item.description: Oprah Winfrey exclusively revealed new details about "AHA," the first-ever immersive journey at the Las Vegas Sphere, coming in 2027.

item.title: About Us
item.description: "60 Minutes" airs Sundays at 7 p.m. ET/PT

item.title: Stella Parton says her sister Dolly was prepared and at peace when she died
item.description: Stella Parton gives insight into her sister Dolly Parton's marriage, makeup habits and views on death in an exclusive CBS News interview.

item.title: Gold Star family calls on Army to release probe of deadly attack on Kuwait base
item.description: Six Americans were killed in the March 1 strike on a tactical operations center in Kuwait.

item.title: Malcolm-Jamal Warner's widow on actor's death: "My body went through shock"
item.description: Tenisha Warner, the widow of "The Cosby Show" actor Malcolm-Jamal Warner, spoke exclusively to "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King about coping with grief one year after his death.

item.title: Tenisha Warner, widow of Malcolm-Jamal Warner, opens up about being a single mom
item.description: Tenisha Warner sat down for an exclusive interview with "CBS Mornings" before a lawsuit over her late husband's estate became public, and discussed her grief and raising her daughter alone.

item.title: Michael Jordan says he was "all in" on NASCAR lawsuit
item.description: In a rare interview, Michael Jordan discusses settling his antitrust fight with NASCAR, his passion for racing and more.
